target: Chiunque parli italiano sa quanto sia bello.
english: Whoever speaks Italian knows how beautiful it is.
tip: Indefinite pronouns/adjectives (qualunque, chiunque, ovunque) take the subjunctive in formal usage.

target: Stavo leggendo e d'improvviso è caduta la luce.
english: I was reading and suddenly the power went out.
tip: Imperfetto progressivo (stavo leggendo) for background + passato prossimo (è caduta) for sudden event.
Here lo stands for a whole idea, not a masculine noun: non lo so means I don't know it (the fact).
In the stare plus gerund progressive, the reflexive pronoun can sit before stare: ti stai divertendo.
Ne replaces a counted noun already understood: quanti ne vuoi means how many of them do you want.
Fidarsi always pairs with di for the person trusted: ci fidiamo di te means we trust you.
Many -ire verbs add -isc- inside the present tense: trasferirsi becomes si trasferisce.
Italian keeps the garment singular even for several people: si tolgono il cappotto, one coat each.
Da plus a present-tense verb marks ongoing time: conosco da anni means I have known her and still do.
Parlare takes di, and ne replaces that di phrase: ne abbiamo parlato means we talked about it.
"Fallo" = fa' + lo – pronoun attaches to shortened form.

english: I'll tell it to you later.
tip: Before another pronoun, vi becomes ve: ve la racconto means I tell it to you.
Reciprocal actions take essere in the past and the participle agrees: ci siamo incontrati.
For a polite Lei command, use the subjunctive form: parli, not parla, in parli piu lentamente.
The informal tu command of an -are verb ends in -a: tu parla, while tu parli is the plain present.
After an infinitive the reflexive pronoun attaches to the end: vestirsi becomes vestirmi.
Dare su means to look out onto: la finestra da sul giardino overlooks the garden.
Here da means through or via, not from: il treno passa da Bologna goes by way of Bologna.

english: I save to buy a house.
tip: Per plus an infinitive means in order to: per comprare una casa means in order to buy a house.

english: Starting tomorrow I'm going on a diet.
tip: Da before a time word means starting from: da domani means from tomorrow onward.

target: Potrebbe spiegarlo di nuovo, per favore?
english: Could you explain that again, please?
tip: "Potrebbe" – formal conditional of potere for polite questions.

target: Le persone che conosco sono simpatiche.
english: The people I know are nice.
tip: Italian keeps che even when English drops that: le persone che conosco means the people I know.

target: Ci svegliamo, ci vestiamo e partiamo.
english: We wake up, get dressed, and leave.
tip: Each reflexive verb needs its own pronoun: ci svegliamo, ci vestiamo, one ci per verb.

target: Benché faccia freddo, usciamo lo stesso.
english: Although it's cold, we're going out anyway.
tip: "Benché" + subjunctive: faccia, not fa.

target: Prendine un altro, questo è rotto.
english: Take another one, this one is broken.
tip: Prendine is prendi plus ne, where ne stands for 'of them': prendine means 'take one of them'.

target: Credo che domani faccia bel tempo.
english: I believe the weather will be nice tomorrow.
tip: Credo che (I believe that) triggers the subjunctive: faccia bel tempo, not fa.

target: La casa in cui vivo è piccola.
english: The house I live in is small.
tip: English drops the pronoun in 'the house I live in', but Italian must keep it: la casa in cui vivo.
With stare plus a gerund, the pronoun can sit before stare (mi sta chiamando) or attach to the gerund (sta chiamandomi). Same meaning.
Avere bisogno takes di. Ne stands in for that di-phrase, so ne ho bisogno means I have need of it.
When a number stands alone without its noun, Italian still needs ne: ne prendo due, literally I take two of them.
